case_name: Homi Rajvansh v State of Maharashtra and others
facts: The appellant, an Indian Revenue Service Officer, joined National Agricultural Co-operative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED), on deputation on 15.07.2003 as an Executive Director.

On 01.10.2003, Respondent No.3 herein-Alok Ranjan took over the charge as the new Managing Director of NAFED and he approved the 1st Non- agricultural tie-up of NAFED on 13.10.2003 in order to diversify NAFED's business activities.

On 20.04.2004, when the Respondent No.3 was scheduled to go for an international tour to Beijing, the appellant was made the officiating Managing Director for 21.04.2004 to 27.04.2004 in order to attend all urgent matters.
In January 2006, a public interest litigation was filed against NAFED before the Delhi High Court on the allegations of misappropriation of funds by its officials in non-agricultural business.
The Government of India, in its reply, stated that CBI enquiry will be conducted. In the affidavit filed by NAFED, it was again reiterated that all the transactions were bona fide.

Anticipating pressure of CBI, Respondent No.3 directed Mr. M.V. Haridas, Manager (Vigilance and Personnel) to lodge a complaint against SGI and, accordingly, a complaint was lodged before the CBI Economic Offences Wing (EOW), Mumbai.

The CBI filed a charge-sheet dated 15.12.2008 against the appellant herein and Respondent No.3 along with other accused for committing offence under Section 120B read with Sections 409, 411,420, 467, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short 'the IPC').

At this stage, Respondent No.3 preferred a petition being Criminal Writ Petition No. 220 of 2010 for discharge before the High Court u/s. 482 of the Code read with Article 226/227 of the Constitution of India.
By impugned order dated 29.06.2012, the High Court accepted the case of Respondent No.3 herein and allowed his petition.
issues: The High Court erred in quashing the complaint against Respondent No.3 without hearing the appellant herein who is a co-accused in the case.
The High Court had over exercised its jurisdiction by holding a summary trial on facts, which is contrary to the law laid down by this Court in catena of judgments.
The High Court committed an error in coming to a finding against the appellant without the appellant being a party in the writ petition filed by Respondent No.3 herein before it.
The High Court committed an error in agreeing with the submissions of Respondent No.3 herein without affording an opportunity of being heard to the appellant.
petitioner_arguments: The High Court erred in quashing the complaint against Respondent No.3 without hearing the appellant herein who is a co-accused in the case.
The High Court had over exercised its jurisdiction by holding a summary trial on facts, which is contrary to the law laid down by this Court in catena of judgments.
The High Court committed an error in coming to a finding against the appellant without the appellant being a party in the writ petition filed by Respondent No.3 herein before it.
The High Court committed an error in agreeing with the submissions of Respondent No.3 herein without affording an opportunity of being heard to the appellant.
respondent_arguments: In the absence of specific material in the charge-sheet about the role of respondent No.3, the High Court is fully justified in quashing the criminal case and discharging him.
There is no categorical finding against the appellant and the High Court has merely reproduced what is stated in the charge sheet and nothing more.
court_reasoning: The allegations that the accused No.2 - Homi Rajvansh, committed the acts in question without the approval of the Managing Director, i.e., the petitioner and without informing him and the allegation that the Managing Director, i.e., the petitioner is responsible for the said acts, cannot go hand in hand together.
The investigation could establish that he had acquired huge properties from the ill-gotten wealth......

Indeed, the allegations against the co-accused Homi Rajvansh are supported by material in the charge sheet, but the very absence of such material, so far as the petitioner is concerned, renders the theory of the petitioner being a party to the alleged conspiracy, unacceptable.
holding: The High Court committed an error in quashing the complaint against Respondent No.3 without hearing the appellant herein who is a co-accused in the case.
The High Court committed an error in coming to a finding against the appellant without the appellant being a party in the writ petition filed by Respondent No.3.
cases_cited: Homi Rajvansh v State of Maharashtra
